# 1 Clement Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_011_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 11 covers Lot — like Abraham before him, praised for hospitality and godliness. The counterexample of Lot's wife introduces *dipsychos* (double-minded) — a word rare in Greek but prominent in the letter of James. The detail "to this day" suggests Clement knows the pillar-of-salt tradition as a visible landmark still pointed out in his time.

The phrase "not in one accord nor in agreement with him" (v.2) describes Lot's wife's spiritual condition — she was not *homophrōn* (of one mind/accord). This is the same vocabulary used of the harmonious animals in the ark (9:4) and will be used for the cosmic order (ch. 20). Discord vs. concord is a structural motif throughout the letter.

---

## Chapter 11

**11:1** Because of his hospitality and godliness Lot was saved out of Sodom, when all the surrounding region was condemned by fire and brimstone; the Lord thereby making manifest that he does not forsake those who hope in him, but delivers to punishment and torment those who are otherwise-minded. [Gen 19]

**11:2** As a sign of this, his wife was left behind; for since her soul was not in accord with his nor in agreement, she became a pillar of salt to this day, that it might be known to all that those who are double-minded and those who doubt the power of God fall under judgment and become a warning to all generations. [Gen 19:26]

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
